response.sql:
WITH valid_patients AS (
    SELECT p.ID, p.SEX
    FROM Patient p
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM Laboratory l
        WHERE l.ID = p.ID AND l.`U-PRO` = '-'
    )
),
patient_stats AS (
    SELECT 
        l.ID,
        AVG(l.PT) as avg_pt,
        AVG(CASE WHEN l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT <> 0 THEN l.ALP / l.GPT END) as avg_ratio
    FROM Laboratory l
    INNER JOIN valid_patients vp ON l.ID = vp.ID
    GROUP BY l.ID
)
SELECT 
    COALESCE(vp.SEX, '') as SEX,
    AVG(ps.avg_pt) as avg_pt,
    AVG(ps.avg_ratio) as avg_ratio
FROM valid_patients vp
INNER JOIN patient_stats ps ON vp.ID = ps.ID
GROUP BY COALESCE(vp.SEX, '')
ORDER BY COALESCE(vp.SEX, '')

assumptions.assumption: Records where GPT is NULL or 0 are excluded when calculating the ALP/GPT ratio per record, consistent with treating them as missing data ('Averages ignore missing values'). Division by zero is thus avoided.

alternatives.interpretation: NULL SEX values may be output as SQL NULL instead of converted to empty string. Both versions treat NULL SEX as a separate group; this alternative preserves NULL in output rather than materializing it as ''.
